doc_verification.detail: Page live at https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/collections/delete-collection (fetched HTML + .md full text via alternate reader; built-in WebFetch was network-restricted but page itself reachable). Version v1.18.x matches target v1.18.0. Endpoint exact. CONTENT FAIL: the page documents ONLY a 200 'successful operation' response (result:boolean) — there is NO 404 response row anywhere on the page or in its .md form. The repo's own OpenAPI source (openapi-collections.ytt.yaml delete: responses #@ response(type("boolean")); openapi.lib.yml response() helper declares only "200" + generic default/4XX ErrorResponse envelope) likewise declares no specific 404 for delete_collection. The assertion half 'DELETE missing => 404' therefore has no doc-text grounding; the constraint description's '(runtime verified)' parenthetical in raw_knowledge.md line 131 applies only to '200 on real delete', not to the 404 half, which is an inference. The doc half 'DELETE existing => 200' IS consistent (documented 200, observed 200 result:true).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix delete_collection [src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:160-178] → dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(CollectionMetaOperations::DeleteCollection) [lib/storage/src/dispatcher.rs] → TableOfContents perform_meta_op → self.delete_collection [toc/collection_meta_ops.rs:78-81 → 211-296] → collections.remove(name) returns None for missing → result=false → Ok(result) [l295] → process_response Ok(_) → HttpResponse::Ok() 200 result:false [src/actix/helpers.rs:62-70]. Read-path asymmetry: get/exists/count/scroll resolve via resolve_name → validate_collection_exists → StorageError::not_found → HttpError 404. The existence check that produces 404 is deliberately applied on reads and deliberately absent on delete.
source_grounding.note: Not validation_absent: the source intentionally implements idempotent delete — missing collection yields Ok(false)→200, with an explicit concurrency comment (collection_create_lock rationale, l273-274) and a disk-cleanup fallback for unloaded collections. No dedicated unit test asserting delete-missing semantics was found (grep in lib/storage/tests and tests/ returned zero hits), and the clone is single-commit (shallow at tag v1.18.0), so design intent rests on in-code comments plus the structural read/delete asymmetry, not on history archaeology.
